title: private-peering-dns-udp-fragmentation-investigation
content:
Quick notes and scratchpad for an ugly class of private deployment networking flakiness: DNS lookups intermittently returning SERVFAIL or truncated responses when clients are routed across a peered VPC + NAT gateway path that traverses a firewall appliance that may be doing MTU clamping / ICMP blackholing. Goal: capture commands tried, observed outputs, working hypothesis, and short reproducible checks so oncall/next-person can continue from here.

Summary:
- Symptom: services in customer private deployment (vpc-a) occasionally fail name resolution for large records (DNS over UDP). Fall back to TCP or HTTP-based discovery sometimes succeeds. Failures correlated with paths that traverse VPC peering -> transit VPC -> third-party firewall appliance in customer network.
- Frequency: ~3-5x / day for this customer during peak (30% query rate to large TXT/CAA/long-EDNS responses).
- Suspected root causes: UDP fragmentation + ICMP unreachable/filtered or incorrect MSS/MTU handling along peering path; EDNS0 UDP size > path MTU triggers fragmentation that is blocked.

Repro steps (lab):
1) From bastion in vpc-a (10.20.5.12) replicate a large DNS response using our internal dns-mock service (port 5053) serving a 1800-byte TXT.
2) tcpdump on bastion and on peering hop, confirm packet size and ICMP messages.
3) use dig + +bufsize and +short to reproduce truncation.

Commands & notable outputs (copied raw):

# on bastion (vpc-a)
$ ping -M do -s 1472 10.1.0.1
PING 10.1.0.1 (10.1.0.1) 1472(1500) bytes of data.
--- 10.1.0.1 ping statistics ---
4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss, time 3003ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.318/0.340/0.376/0.020 ms
\n# dig against dns-mock (UDP) returns TC sometimes
$ dig @10.30.2.8 -p 5053 big-txt.example +bufsize=4096 +time=2 +tries=2
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> @10.30.2.8 -p 5053 big-txt.example +bufsize=4096
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; Truncated, retrying in TCP...\n\n# tcpdump on bastion while reproducing UDP query (showing large UDP len)
$ sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/dnsfrag.pcap port 53 and host 10.30.2.8 &

# tcpdump excerpt (observed)
19:08:12.123456 IP 10.20.5.12.54321 > 10.30.2.8.53: 12345+ A? big-txt.example. (49)
19:08:12.123789 IP 10.30.2.8.53 > 10.20.5.12.54321: 12345 q: 1  r: 0  TXT "(first chunk)" (1480)
19:08:12.124001 IP 10.30.2.8.53 > 10.20.5.12.54321: 12345 q: 1  r: 0  TXT "(second chunk)" (420)
\n# On an intermediate hop (transit firewall) we saw ICMP frag-needed (captured via mirror)
12:03:41.999999 ICMP 192.0.2.5 > 10.20.5.12: fragmentation needed - mtu 1400
\nObservations:
- Upstream server emits EDNS0 response size ~1500-2000 bytes (we tested with our mock).
- Path MTU between servers appears to be ~1400 on one leg, but PMTU discovery fails: either ICMP frag-needed is being dropped by the firewall or source isn't reacting.
- Bursts where dig returns 'Truncated' are coincident with the MTU mismatch and absence of TCP retry success in some clients (some libraries don't fall back to TCP cleanly).
- When we forced +bufsize=512, UDP responses succeed consistently.

Quick tests run and results:
- sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward and rp_filter checked on customer VM: all default (ip_forward=1 when routing), rp_filter=0 on transit.
- iptables: no explicit rule dropping ICMP type 3/4, but the third-party firewall has a 'deny ICMP' default.
- curl to remote service unaffected; only DNS UDP path impacted.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) PMTU blackhole: firewall blocks ICMP frag-needed, causing sender to continue sending >MTU UDP fragments which get dropped at next hop. Some DNS servers rely on fragmentation to deliver large UDP answers and don't set EDNS0 buffer to safe size.
2) Firewall is rewriting DF bit incorrectly on forwarded packets, or NATd packet sizes are changed causing fragmentation behavior mismatch.
3) Peering route asymmetry: return path passes through a device with a lower MTU that never signals back, so some queries succeed (short answers) and large ones fail.
4) Misconfigured DNAT on NAT gateway doing MSS clamping for TCP but not adjusting UDP behavior.

Mitigations tried (and result):
- Force EDNS0 bufsize 512 on resolver (works but not ideal for large records) -- temporary config change applied to customer-side stub resolver.
- Add resolver fallback to TCP (we added a library-level retry in our SDK) — mitigates app errors but increases latency and load.
- Asked network team to permit ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag-needed) through the firewall. They reported "deny all ICMP" policy and are evaluating exception (pending).
- Adjusted NAT gateway MTU to 1400 as an experiment; reduced failures but introduced some unrelated throughput regressions on other flows. Reverted.

Useful follow-ups / next steps:
- Run a controlled PMTU discovery sweep end->end while capturing on both ends + on firewall appliance to confirm where frag-needed is lost. Commands: tracepath, scapy script to send increasing UDP sizes while logging ICMP replies.
- Ask vendor for firewall logs for icmp type 3; check if there is a mode to "allow frag-needed" or to enable proper PMTU proxying.
- Add short-term conservative EDNS0 bufsize policy for this customer's resolvers (512) and monitor errors/latency.
- Instrument our resolver library to record when UDP truncated + TCP fallback happens (metric).
- Create a small 'dns-large' test in the e2e suite that intentionally requests >1400 byte responses and asserts either successful UDP or TC->TCP behavior within 200ms.

Notes for next person picking up:
- Packet captures are in /var/tmp/customer-1234/dumps/ (bastion + mirrored firewall interface). File prefix dnsfrag-*.pcap. Use Wireshark to reassemble and look for 'ICMP Port unreachable' vs 'Fragmentation needed'.
- Key ticket: ENG-5721 contains customer network diagrams and vendor contact thread.
- We have a mitigated but not ideal config change on the customer's stub resolver (EDNS0 512) deployed as of 2026-02-12; rollback after vendor fix planned.

Commands to re-run (copy+paste):
# quick PMTU trace
$ sudo tracepath -n 10.30.2.8
# UDP probe loop (python scapy pseudo)
$ python3 - <<'PY'
from scapy.all import *
for s in [1200,1300,1400,1450,1500,1600]:
    pkt = IP(dst='10.30.2.8')/UDP(sport=33333,dport=53)/Raw(b'A'* (s-28))
    resp = sr1(pkt, timeout=2, verbose=0)
    print(s, '->', 'resp' if resp else 'noresp')
PY

Anything else:
- I noted the customer firewall vendor has a historical bug where it drops ICMP frag-needed if deep-packet-inspection policy matched. Asked SE to pull known issues.
- If firewall vendor can't be changed, long-term fix is to ensure resolvers use smaller EDNS0 or support robust TCP fallback with caching to reduce load.

End of scratchpad.

-- aisha
